questions.question: Which of the following mountain peaks is a part of the Himalayas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kamet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kamet** is the second highest mountain in the Garhwal region of Uttarakhand, India.
 
• It is a part of the **Himalayas** and specifically located in the Zanskar Range.
 
• Kamet stands at an elevation of **7,756 meters (25,446 feet)**.
 
• It is the third highest peak in India, outside of the Karakoram range.
 
• The peak was first summited in 1931 by Frank Smythe, Eric Shipton, and R.L. Holdsworth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Himalayas**

 
 
• The Himalayas are a mountain range in Asia, separating the plains of the Indian subcontinent from the Tibetan Plateau.
 
• The range has some of the planet's highest peaks, including the very highest, Mount Everest in Nepal.
 
• The Himalayas span five countries: Bhutan, India, Nepal, China, and Pakistan.
 
• The name "Himalaya" means "abode of snow" in Sanskrit, reflecting the vast amounts of snow and ice that cover the range.
 
 
 
• **Zanskar Range**
 
 
• The Zanskar Range is a mountain range in the union territory of Ladakh that separates Zanskar from Ladakh.
 
• It is a sub-range of the Himalayas and stretches from the eastern part of Ladakh to the Himachal Pradesh border.
 
• The range has many high peaks, with Kamet being one of the most prominent.
 
 
 
• **Mountaineering in India**
 
 
• India offers a variety of mountaineering opportunities, with the Himalayas being a prime destination.
 
• The Indian Mountaineering Foundation (IMF) is the apex body for mountaineering and allied sports in India.
 
• Several high-altitude peaks in India are popular among climbers, including Nanda Devi, Kanchenjunga, and Kamet.
 
 
 
• **Climatic Conditions**
 
 
• The Himalayas play a crucial role in influencing the climate of the Indian subcontinent, particularly the monsoon.
 
• The high peaks block cold winds from Central Asia, keeping South Asia warmer in winter.
 
• The range also causes orographic precipitation, leading to diverse ecosystems and weather patterns across the region.

questions.question: Which plateaus are very fertile because they are rich in black soil that is very good for farming?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deccan lava plateau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Deccan lava plateau is known for its **black soil**, also called regur soil, which is ideal for growing cotton and other crops.
 
• This region is one of the most fertile areas in India, making it a crucial agricultural zone.
 
• The black soil in the Deccan lava plateau retains moisture, which is beneficial for farming even during dry seasons.
 
• The soil is rich in essential nutrients like calcium carbonate, magnesium, potash, and lime, which support diverse agricultural activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Black Soil**

 
 
• Also known as regur soil, black soil is formed from volcanic rocks and lava-flow areas.
 
• This type of soil is highly moisture-retentive and is rich in iron, lime, calcium, potassium, aluminum, and magnesium.
 
• Black soil is predominantly found in the Deccan plateau, including parts of Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is especially suited for growing cotton, and thus it is also called "cotton soil."
 
 
 
• **Deccan Plateau**
 
 
• The Deccan Plateau is a large plateau in western and southern India, covering about 500,000 square kilometers.
 
• It is bounded by the Western Ghats on the west, the Eastern Ghats on the east, and the Satpura and Vindhya ranges to the north.
 
• The plateau is composed of ancient crystalline, igneous, and metamorphic rocks.
 
• The region experiences a semi-arid climate with distinct dry and wet seasons.
 
 
 
• **Fertility of Soil**
 
 
• Soil fertility refers to the ability of soil to sustain agricultural plant growth, i.e., to provide plant habitat and result in sustained and consistent yields of high quality.
 
• Fertile soil contains essential nutrients for plant growth, including nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium.
 
• Other factors influencing soil fertility include soil structure, organic matter content, pH level, and moisture retention capacity.
 
• In agricultural practices, soil fertility is enhanced by adding organic and inorganic fertilizers, crop rotation, and other soil management practices.

questions.question: The peninsular plateau of India was a part of which continent earlier?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Africa**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The peninsular plateau of India was once a part of the ancient supercontinent known as Gondwana.
 
• Gondwana included regions that are now part of Africa, South America, Antarctica, Australia, and the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Over millions of years, the tectonic plates drifted apart, leading to the present-day geographical formations.
 
• This separation and movement of the tectonic plates is explained by the theory of continental drift proposed by Alfred Wegener.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of continental drift was further developed into the theory of plate tectonics, which explains the movement of Earth's lithospheric plates.
 
• India's collision with the Eurasian plate led to the formation of the Himalayas.
 
• The peninsular plateau is characterized by its stable geological structure and is one of the oldest landmasses on Earth.
 
• The plateau is rich in minerals and has significant geological and ecological importance.

questions.question: Geologically, which of the following physiographic divisions of India is supposed to be one of the most stable land blocks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the peninsular plateau**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Peninsular Plateau

 
 
• ​Geologically, the physiographic division of India that is supposed to be one of the most stable land blocks is the Peninsular Plateau.
 
• A tableland made up of ancient crystalline, igneous, and metamorphic rocks are known as the Peninsular plateau.
 
• It belongs to the oldest landmass because it was created by the fracturing and drifting of the Gondwana region.
 
• The vast Deccan Plateau, which can be roughly defined as the peninsular area between these mountain ranges that is south of the Narmada river, is situated between the Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats in southern India.
 
• It is a rocky environment highlighted by stones (2,000 ft).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• India's most valuable metal reserves, including those for iron, bauxite, mica, gold, copper, etc., are located in the peninsular plateau.
 
• The peninsular plateau is where renowned mines like Kolar, Bailadila, Singhbum, and Korba are situated.
 
• The peninsular plateau's climate and black soil make it an ideal place for the cultivation of cotton. Since ancient times, cotton has been essential to the trade and economic growth of India.
 
• The peninsular plateau is known for its rough topography and slips.

questions.question: The Coromandel plain is located in the _______ direction of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Southern.**__

__
 
• The Coromandel plain is located in the **Southern **direction of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Coromandel Coast** is the southeastern coast region of the Indian subcontinent, bounded by the Utkal Plains to the north, the Bay of Bengal to the east, the Kaveri delta to the south, and the Eastern Ghats to the west.
 
• The Coromandal coast extends over an area of about **22,800** square kilometers.
 
• It may also include the southeastern coast of the island of Sri Lanka.
 
• The coast is generally low and punctuated by the deltas of several large rivers, including the **Kaveri, Palar, Penner, and Krishna **which rise in the highlands of the Western Ghats and flow across the Deccan Plateau to drain into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The alluvial plains created by these rivers are **fertile and favour agriculture**.
 
• The coast is also known for its ports and harbours **Pulicat, Chennai, Sadras, Pondicherry, Karaikal, Cuddalore, Tranquebar, Nagore, and Nagapattinam** which take advantage of their close proximity with regions rich in natural and mineral resources **(like the Chhattisgarh belt and the mines of Golconda and Kolar) and/or good transport infrastructure.**
 
• The Coromandel Coast falls in the **rain shadow of the Western Ghats** and receives a good deal less rainfall during the **summer southwest monsoon**, which contributes heavily to rainfall in the rest of India.
 
• The region averages **800 mm/year,** most of which falls between October and December.
 
• During the winter season, north-east trade winds **prevail over India.**
 
• The Coromandal coast receives winter rainfall because of the **retreating monsoon**
 
• The North-east Monsoon winds pass over the **Bay of Bengal.**
 
• They blow from land to sea and hence, for most parts of the country, it is a** dry season.**
 
• These cause **winter rains** over the plains and **snowfall** in the mountains.
 
• It is because in this region these winds blow from sea to land, thereby carrying moisture along with them.
 
• North-East monsoon is also known as **'October Heat'.**

questions.question: Which sub-division of Himalayas are famous for Karewa formations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kashmir Himalayas**__

__
 
• The sub-division of Himalayas famous for **Karewa formations** is the **Kashmir Himalayas**.
 
• Karewas are lacustrine deposits (deposits in lake beds) found in the Kashmir Valley.

questions.question: ________ zone is generally defined as an environment with moderate rainfall throughout the year or parts of the year, with sporadic dry, mild to hot summers and cool to cold winters.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Temperate Zone**

 
 
• Between the** tropics and the polar regions** is where the t**emperate zone primarily exists**.
 
• There are typically **four distinct seasons**, with a **vast variation in temperatures and precipitation**.
 
• It is generally defined as an e**nvironment with moderate rainfall throughout the year or parts of the year, with sporadic dry, mild to hot summers and cool to cold winters**. 
 
• The** continental United States, the majority of Canada and Europe, Central Asia, southern South America, and southern Australia** are among the areas that are exclusively covered in the **temperate zone**.
 
• The average temperature of the temperate zone lies between zero and 20°C.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tropical Zone**

 
 
• The areas of the** planet closest to the equator and between the Tropics of Cancer in the north and Capricorn in the south are known as tropical regions**.
 
• The average temperature in the tropics ranges from **25 to 28 degrees Celsius (77 to 82 degrees Fahrenheit)**.
 
 
 
• **Dry Zone**
 
 
• The** sub-humid regions of the nation that receive 75 cm to 100 cm of rainfall **(and hence have moisture deficiency for two-thirds of the year) and the** semi-arid regions that receive 30 cm to 75 cm of rainfall are considered dry-land zones**.
 
 
 
• **Continental Zone**
 
 
• The region with the** largest geographic scope is known as the Continental Zone (CON)**, which also encompasses portions of the** lower hills on the ALS border as well as the plains and lowlands of Central and Eastern Europe and the Balkans**.
 
• The weather is continental, with** wide annual temperature variations and heavy summertime precipitation**.

questions.question: The Kumaon Himalayas lie between which two rivers?

• **Kumaun Himalayas, a west-central section of the Himalayas in northern India, extending 200 miles (320 km) from the Sutlej River east to the Kali River**__.

• The part of the Himalayas lying between the **rivers Indus and Satluj is known as Punjab Himalayas**.
 
• **The part of the Himalayas lying between the rivers Kali and Teesta is known as Nepal Himalayas**.
 
• The part of the Himalayas lying between the rivers **Teesta and Dihang is known as Assam Himalayas**.
 
• The part of the Himalayas lying between the rivers **Satluj and Kali is known as Kumaon Himalayas**.
 
 
 
• The main Himalayan river systems are those of the Indus and the Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna system.
 
• The Indus, which is one of the great rivers of the world, rises near Mansarovar in Tibet and flows through India, and thereafter through Pakistan, and finally falls in the Arabian Sea near Karachi.
 
• The Brahmaputra marks the easternmost boundary of the Himalayas. Beyond the Dihang gorge, the Himalayas bend sharply to the south and spread along the eastern boundary of India.
 
• **To the south of the main Himalayas lies the Pir Panjal Range** at an average height of 5,000 meters (16,000 ft).
 
• From Gulmarg, in the northwest, it follows the southern rim of the Kashmir valley to the Banihal Pass.
 
• Here the **Pir Panjal meets the ridgeline that separates the Kashmir valley from the Warvan Valley**.

__
 
• **India lost a large proportion of cotton growing area to Pakistan during the partition.**
 
• The industry suffered in several ways:
 
 
• India’s share in the **output of raw cotton in undivided India was about 60%**, while the corresponding share in the mill output was as high as 9**5%.**
 
• Secondly, the **areas growing high-quality long and medium staple cotton went to West Punjab and Sind.**
 
• Thirdly, **India lost a sizeable amount of its internal market **because of the partition.
 
• The country also** lost its earlier advantage as an exporter.**
 
 
 
• Approximately 65 percent of Pakistan's cotton is grown in Punjab as the region has dry conditions.
 
• The rest is grown in Sindh, which has a more humid climate, with the negligible area under cotton in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan.
 
• **During the partition these areas went into Pakistan, hence India lost a huge proportion of its cotton production.​**

• Cotton is a** tropical or sub-tropical crop grown **in semi-arid areas of the country (mainly in the Deccan Plateau).
 
• A hard frost is injurious to cotton cultivation and it** requires at least 210 frost-free days.**
 
• **Only light rainfall (50 to 100 centimetres) is preferred.**
 
• Cotton can also be cultivated under irrigated conditions.
 
• It** **requires high temperature and bright sunshine for its growth.
 
• Cotton requires a clear sky during the flowering stage.
 
• A light well-drained soil capable of retaining moisture is ideally suited for the cultivation of the crop.
 
• **Black cotton soil is preferred.**
 
• It is a** **Kharif crop and requires 6 to 8 months to mature.
 
 
 
• Now,** India is the leading cotton-producing country.**

questions.question: Terrace farming is commonly practiced in which of the following regions of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Himalayan region**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Terrace farming is a traditional agricultural practice in the **Himalayan region** due to its steep slopes and mountainous terrain.
 
• It helps in reducing soil erosion and water runoff, which are common issues in hilly areas.
 
• Terrace farming allows for the cultivation of various crops such as rice, maize, and potatoes, which are essential for the local populations.
 
• This method of farming is crucial for maximizing arable land area and ensuring food security in the Himalayan region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terrace Farming**

 
 
• Terrace farming is a method of carving steps or terraces into the slopes of hilly or mountainous regions to create flat areas for agriculture.
 
• This technique helps in retaining soil moisture, preventing soil erosion, and making efficient use of water.
 
• It is commonly used in areas with uneven terrain where traditional farming methods are not feasible.
 
 
 
• **Himalayan Region**
 
 
• The Himalayas are a mountain range in South Asia, separating the plains of the Indian subcontinent from the Tibetan Plateau.
 
• The region is known for its high peaks, including Mount Everest, the highest point on Earth.
 
• The climate and topography of the Himalayas make terrace farming an essential practice for local agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Soil Erosion**
 
 
• Soil erosion is the process by which the top layer of soil is removed by natural forces such as wind and water.
 
• It is a significant issue in hilly areas where heavy rainfall and steep slopes can lead to rapid loss of fertile soil.
 
• Terrace farming helps to mitigate soil erosion by creating flat surfaces that reduce the speed of water runoff.
 
 
 
• **Water Runoff**
 
 
• Water runoff refers to the flow of water, typically from precipitation, over the surface of the land.
 
• In hilly regions, rapid water runoff can lead to soil erosion and loss of nutrients from the soil.
 
• Terracing helps to slow down water runoff and allows for better absorption of water by the soil.
